item: A write-gate waiter looks again every second, so a wake-up lost in release (or in the finally of a gave-up acquire) costs one step and not the rest of the process
refs: PR #1448; open item L2 of PR #1435; coordinator 17 Oct (order: M, the D note, L2)
summary: WriterGate.release clears the owner and then wakes the head of the queue; a KeyboardInterrupt or MemoryError inside that wake-up (forced in the new tests, on the real release and on the wake-up of a gave-up acquire's finally) left the gate free and the head asleep on a condition nobody notifies, and acquire's wait had no timeout, so every later writer queued behind it until restart. acquire now waits in steps of _WAKE_STEP_S (1.0 s, chosen, not tuned: nothing measured argues for it over 0.25 or 2): untimed waits step by it, bounded waits by min(time left, step), in the same loop shape the interrupt pins check. Not a timeout (an acquire without one waits as long as the gate is held; pinned) and a bounded acquire still gives up at its own deadline. Cost measured: 49 queued writers behind a 20 s hold, 0.0002 s CPU before and 0.0366 s after (980 wake-ups, about 37 us each, 0.18 percent of a core). Red-without: on the old waits with the constant defined the injection tests of both paths fail on behaviour (the writer never gets through) and the pin fails (on the module literally as it was they fail earlier, at the setattr of the missing constant); a control per path with the step stubbed out leaves the writer asleep. Side effect found by the read: an acquire with a timeout of infinity or above the platform limit used to raise OverflowError from the wait after joining the queue, and the step makes it wait normally. Named: a failure in the wake-up skips the measuring of that one release; the real-signal rate of the loss was not measured.
